record.paper_title: Open Questions in Cosmic-Ray Research at Ultrahigh Energies
record.original_question: What is the physical origin of the knee, second-knee or iron-knee, and ankle features in the cosmic-ray spectrum between about 10^15 and 10^18 eV, and at which feature does the transition from Galactic cosmic rays to an extragalactic component begin? In particular, are the knee features produced by propagation changes, by maximum energies of Galactic sources such as supernova remnants, or by another mechanism?

evidence.quote: The cosmic-ray spectrum features three distinct spectral breaks in the energy range between1015−1018eV. In order of increasing energy, these are the “knee”, “second-knee” (or “iron-knee”) , and “ankle”, illustrated in Figure 12.
The physical origin of the knee feature remains unclear. Both a propagation and sources maximum energy origin of this feature remain viable candidates.
However, whether SNRs are actually able to accelerate up to the knee energy (3 PeV) remains an open question.
If the interpretation of these observational results is correct, the onset of this new light component marks the beginning of an extragalactic component in the arriving CR ﬂux.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and research papers (PDG 2024 cosmic-ray review, arXiv:2411.17881, A&A 2025 papers, and 2026 propagation studies) continue to debate whether the knee is due to Galactic source maximum energies (e.g. SNRs) or to propagation/escape effects, and whether the Galactic-to-extragalactic transition occurs at the second knee or at the ankle. No consensus has been reached, and competing ankle, dip, and mixed-composition models remain viable.

status_evidence.title: PDG 2024 review: Cosmic Rays
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses knee, second knee, and ankle features and the still-uncertain Galactic-to-extragalactic transition.
status_evidence.claim: The origin of the knee features and the location of the Galactic/extragalactic transition remain debated as of 2024.

status_evidence.title: The transition from Galactic to extragalactic cosmic rays (arXiv:2411.17881)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews competing models for the high-energy end of the Galactic cosmic-ray spectrum and the transition to extragalactic sources.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple scenarios for the transition (at second knee or ankle) are still considered viable.

status_evidence.title: Joint constraint on the propagation origin of the cosmic-ray spectral knee
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work testing whether the knee can be explained by propagation effects rather than source maximum energy.
status_evidence.claim: Whether the knee is propagation-induced or source-maximum-energy-induced is still under active investigation.
